Use section 2's de-duplication check (grep -B1) before inserting, so a unit already marked is skipped. (3) IMPORTANT AND UNUSUAL, specific to req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md itself (this file is IN this chunk's scope, per OQ-4's resolution quoted in context.requirement_text): section 4 of that file contains two worked 'before'/'after' examples, each showing a real citation with and without the marker, specifically to illustrate the convention mechanically. These are NOT a case of an intentionally-unmarked negative example that must stay unmarked -- they are live citations of real R-Co paths (the cursor.zig/field_grants.zig SOURCE: line, and the identity.ex moduledoc paragraph) reproduced inside this design doc's own body text, and per OQ-4's resolution they get marked like any other citation in this file. Concretely: section 4's 'Before' code fence blocks (lines ~252-257 and ~285-292 in the source as read this session -- re-locate by content, not line number, since your own edits will shift them) are themselves quoted **inside a fenced code block** that is demonstrating what an UNMARKED citation looks like elsewhere in the codebase -- that fenced block's CONTENT must NOT be edited (it is quoting docs/requirements.yaml's and identity.ex's actual current unmarked text, used as the illustrative 'before' state; editing it would corrupt the worked example's own meaning, since the 'before' fence is supposed to show what existed prior to REQ-238/239 applying the convention elsewhere). The 'After' fences immediately following each already show the correct marked-up result and also must NOT be re-edited (they are already correct, already contain the marker). What DOES need marking under this chunk's own scope is any OTHER .zig citation in req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md's own **prose** (not inside a fenced before/after illustration) -- reread the whole file for citations outside section 4's fences (e.g. the file's own running prose in sections 0, 1, 6 that names .zig paths/counts inline, such as section 1's phrasing-variety table and section 6's chunking tables, which quote things like 'partition_maintenance.zig', 'dlq.zig', 'cursor.zig', etc. as documentation of what OTHER files look like -- these are citations of citations, i.e. this design doc quoting examples, not this doc's own provenance claims about R-Co code it ported). Read section 2's citation-unit rule carefully: only citations that would themselves need REQ-237's marker if they lived in their original file are candidates; a table CELL inside section 1's phrasing-variety survey table that merely reproduces another file's text as a worked example is analogous to section 4's fences (illustrative, not a live citation belonging to this file) and should NOT be marked. If genuinely ambiguous whether a specific passage is a live citation of this file's own provenance vs. an illustrative quotation of another file's phrasing, flag it explicitly in result.issues as MINOR with the exact line/passage rather than guessing either way -- do not silently resolve it. (4) After all insertions, for every file: re-run `grep -c '\.zig' <file>` and confirm the count is UNCHANGED (marker insertion adds lines, never deletes/alters .zig-bearing lines) -- report before/after per file. (5) Run `grep -rc 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' <the 9 files>` summed, before (should be 0 unless a prior run already marked de-duplication targets, unlikely here) and after -- quote the exact increase. (6) Sample at least 9 citations across at least 5 different files (or every citation if fewer exist) showing a byte-identical path/text diff with only the marker line added -- quote the diffs. (7) Confirm via `git diff --stat` that CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/migration/README.md, and every lib/letflow/design/ file OUTSIDE this chunk's 9-file list are untouched. (8) Confirm via `grep -rnE 'unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co' <the 9 files>` before and after (byte-identical expected) that no deliberate-divergence note was altered. (9) Flip REQ-271's status from in_progress to done in docs/requirements.yaml. (10) Append a 'done' event to docs/status/requirement_status.v10.yaml (current volume; append after its last entry, do not rewrite prior ones) with a real UTC timestamp from the clock, summarizing marker counts and the req237-self-scope handling from step 3 above.
